subtitle: A lens of glass in a kingdom of hills

panels.shot: low-angle interior wide of a dim royal chamber, one side stacked with scrolls and ledgers, the other side filled with a bulky wooden camera and glass plates glowing in a shaft of light
panels.action: Bir Chandra Manikya stands between ledgers of state and a looming wooden camera, one hand resting on each, framed by the arches of Ujjayanta Palace as late sunlight streams through dust-filled air.

dialogue.text: In the hill kingdom of Tripura, Maharaja Bir Chandra Manikya dared to rule with glass and light, turning a palace chamber into one of India’s earliest royal photo factories.

i18n.hi: पहाड़ी राज्य त्रिपुरा में महाराजा वीरचंद्र माणिक्य ने काँच और रोशनी से राज किया, महल के एक कमरे को भारत की शुरुआती शाही फोटो फैक्टरियों में बदल दिया।

panels.shot: bird's-eye view of Agartala and the Ujjayanta compound, framed against distant hills, with small colonial-era buildings and dusty roads beginning to form a grid
panels.action: From above the Ujjayanta royal compound, young Bir Chandra Manikya surveys Agartala’s emerging streets and scattered tiled roofs, the palace standing like a white island amid forest and fields.

dialogue.text: It was the late nineteenth century. Steamships shook the seas, telegraphs stitched continents, and in the hill capital of Agartala a Manikya king watched modernity creep toward his forested realm.

i18n.hi: उन्नीसवीं सदी का आख़िरी दौर था। भाप के जहाज़ समुद्र हिला रहे थे, तार दुनिया जोड़ रहे थे, और आगतला की पहाड़ी राजधानी में एक माणिक्य राजा देख रहा था कि नया ज़माना उसके जंगलों की तरफ़ बढ़ रहा है।

panels.shot: medium interior of a royal office, table crowded with British printed reports, handwritten Persian records and a rolled city plan
panels.action: Bir Chandra Manikya sits at a heavy desk in Ujjayanta, brow furrowed, comparing a neat British municipal report with his own stacked revenue records, while an ink-stained map of Agartala lies unrolled before him.

dialogue.text: Between company reports and ancient royal records, Bir Chandra saw a strange double world: one measured in surveys and minutes, the other in old tribute and temple lists. He knew the hill state must bridge them.

i18n.hi: कम्पनी की फ़ाइलों और प्राचीन राज-दस्तावेज़ों के बीच वीरचंद्र ने दोहरी दुनिया देखी: एक नाप-तौल और मिनटों की, दूसरी नज़राने और देवालय सूचियों की। वह समझ गया, पहाड़ी रियासत को दोनों के बीच पुल बनना होगा।

panels.shot: wide shot of an early council chamber with nobles and officials seated on mats and chairs in a hybrid setting
panels.action: Inside a council hall with both cane mats and imported chairs, Bir Chandra Manikya stands at the center, pointing to a sketch of streets and drains while older courtiers watch with mixed curiosity and doubt.

dialogue.speaker: bir_chandra_manikya
dialogue.text: Agartala must be more than a camp of huts. It shall be a planned town.

i18n.hi: आगतला सिर्फ़ झोपड़ियों का डेरा नहीं रहेगा। यह अब बसाया हुआ शहर बनेगा।

panels.shot: street-level wide of workers laying out roads, digging drains, and erecting simple civic buildings
panels.action: Bare-chested laborers align stones for a road under the watch of a scribe with a ledger, while masons raise a modest civic building whose walls still smell of fresh lime.

dialogue.text: In 1871, Agartala’s first municipal body took shape. Roads gained drains, markets gained order, and the royal compound looked out over a town that now had minutes, bylaws and a civic name.

i18n.hi: १८७१ में आगतला की पहली नगरपालिका बनी। सड़कों को नालियाँ मिलीं, बाज़ारों को क़ायदा, और राजमहल के अहाते से अब एक ऐसा नगर दिखता था जिसके पास मिनट्स, क़ानून और अपना शहरी नाम था।

panels.shot: interior wide of a new classroom with blackboard and benches, seen through a doorway
panels.action: Through an open doorway, Bir Chandra Manikya watches boys in simple cloth sit at wooden benches under a hanging slate board, while a teacher writes English and Bengali letters in chalk.

dialogue.text: Two decades later, in 1890, Umakanta Academy opened its doors with Western-style classes. For the first time in Tripura, a royal charter and a timetable marched in step.

i18n.hi: दो दशक बाद, १८९० में, उमाकान्त अकादमी खुली, पश्चिमी ढंग की कक्षाओं के साथ। पहली बार त्रिपुरा में शाही फ़रमान और टाइमटेबल कदम से कदम मिला कर चले।

panels.shot: close-up of Bir Chandra holding a letter embossed with a Calcutta seal, lamplight catching his thoughtful face
panels.action: By a brass lamp, Bir Chandra Manikya holds a folded letter with a Calcutta address and a faint engraving of a camera, his eyes tracing the neat English script as shadows flicker on the wall.

dialogue.text: Yet Bir Chandra’s curiosity went beyond ledgers and syllabi. From Calcutta came whispers of a new magic—photographs that trapped faces, temples and clouds on fragile plates of glass.

i18n.hi: पर वीरचंद्र की जिज्ञासा हिसाब-किताब और पाठ्यक्रम से आगे थी। कलकत्ता से नई जादू की चर्चा आई—ऐसी तस्वीरें जो चेहरों, मंदिरों और बादलों को नाज़ुक काँच पर क़ैद कर देतीं।

panels.shot: cutaway to a Calcutta photographic salon, then back to an imagined overlay over his face, creating a visual echo
panels.action: In his mind’s eye, Bir Chandra envisions a Calcutta studio where a European photographer adjusts a tripod and a Bengali clerk dusts a glass plate, the faint reflection of this vision shimmering over his own focused gaze.

dialogue.speaker: bir_chandra_manikya
dialogue.text: If they can fix Calcutta on glass, can I not fix Tripura too?

i18n.hi: अगर वे कलकत्ता को काँच पर पकड़ सकते हैं, तो क्या मैं त्रिपुरा को नहीं पकड़ सकता?

panels.shot: interior wide of a long palace room being cleared, servants carrying out furniture while a carpenter measures space
panels.action: In a vaulted palace chamber, servants haul out carved couches while a carpenter measures the floor, and Bir Chandra Manikya gestures to the high windows, already imagining them as sources of controlled light.

dialogue.text: He chose a chamber in Ujjayanta and emptied it of cushions and gossip. Here, instead of royal betting and music, he planned benches, chemicals and a heavy wooden camera—the palace Foto ka Karkhana.

i18n.hi: उसने उज्जयन्त महल का एक कक्ष चुना, गद्दे और गपशप हटवा दी। जहाँ पहले जुआ और संगीत था, वहाँ अब बेंचें, केमिकल और भारी लकड़ी का कैमरा बसाया गया—महल का फ़ोटो का कारख़ाना।

panels.shot: medium shot inside the photo studio, with the camera prominently in foreground and racks of glass plates behind
panels.action: Under a flood of north light, a polished wooden camera on a sturdy tripod dominates the room, flanked by racks of blank glass plates and trays, while Bir Chandra Manikya in simple robes leans in with eager concentration.

dialogue.text: Unlike many princes who posed beneath cameras, Bir Chandra stood behind one. He learned the weight of lenses, the patience of plates and the strange chemistry that turned darkness into images.

i18n.hi: बहुत से राजा कैमरे के सामने खड़े होते थे, वीरचंद्र कैमरे के पीछे खड़ा हुआ। उसने लेंस का वज़न सीखा, प्लेटों का सब्र सीखा और वह अजीब रसायन, जो अँधेरे को तस्वीर बना देता था।

panels.shot: dim interior close-up of his hands tilting a glass plate over a tray of solution, with faint reflections
panels.action: In the dim glow of a shaded lamp, Bir Chandra’s steady hands lower a glass plate into a shallow tray of developer, faint outlines of a face beginning to bloom like a ghost across its surface.

dialogue.speaker: bir_chandra_manikya
dialogue.text: Steady. A kingdom has waited centuries; it can wait a few breaths more.

i18n.hi: ठहरो… यह रियासत सदियों से इंतज़ार कर रही है, कुछ साँस और सही।

panels.shot: wide shot of the studio now active: a noble seated, a tribal elder, and palace women, all being arranged for portraits
panels.action: The Foto ka Karkhana hums as Bir Chandra adjusts the pose of a bearded noble, while in the background a tribal elder and veiled palace women wait calmly, every posture held for the long seconds of exposure.

dialogue.text: He used the studio not only for royal self-regard, but to collect the faces of his court and subjects. Nobles, officials, elders and kin became patient partners in a slow, standing act of documentation.

i18n.hi: उसने स्टूडियो को सिर्फ़ अपने शाही चित्रों के लिए नहीं, बल्कि दरबार और प्रजा के चेहरे समेटने के लिए भी खोला। अमीर, अफ़सर, बुज़ुर्ग और रिश्तेदार, सब इस धीमी, खड़े रहने वाली दस्तावेज़ी रस्म के साथी बने।

panels.shot: medium shot of Bir Chandra arranging a backdrop painted with a temple and then another with a colonial building, side by side
panels.action: Bir Chandra Manikya stands between two painted backdrops, one showing a local shrine and hills, the other a straight colonnaded building, adjusting their cloth edges as if weighing the worlds they represent.

dialogue.text: Many Indian rulers sought portraits in British studios. Bir Chandra instead built his own, letting Tripura’s shrines and new civic facades share the same frame, the same light, the same glass.

i18n.hi: बहुत से भारतीय राजा अपने चित्र अंग्रेज़ी स्टूडियो में बनवाते थे। वीरचंद्र ने अपना स्टूडियो बसाया, ताकि त्रिपुरा के देवालय और नए नागरिक मकान एक ही फ़्रेम, एक ही रोशनी, एक ही काँच में आएँ।

panels.shot: wide shot of Kharchi Puja grounds outside, seen from slightly above, with a crowd and shrines, and Bir Chandra observing from a respectful distance
panels.action: Beyond the palace walls, the Kharchi Puja of the Chaturdasha Devata unfolds in open grounds, with decorated shrines and a thick crowd, while Bir Chandra stands at a shaded edge, watching priests and people move in a widening circle.

dialogue.text: In those same years, Kharchi Puja of the fourteen deities grew into a public spectacle. State ritual stepped into open space, even as within the palace a king learned to freeze such moments on plates.

i18n.hi: उन्हीं सालों में चौदह देवताओं की ख़ारची पूजा बड़ा सार्वजनिक उत्सव बनी। राज्य की रस्में खुले मैदानों में आईं, और महल के भीतर एक राजा ने इन्हीं पलों को काँच की प्लेटों पर रोकना सीखा।

panels.shot: interior medium shot of Bir Chandra photographing a Kharchi-related object or priest inside the studio, not the ritual itself
panels.action: Inside the studio, a priest in simple cloth sits upright while Bir Chandra adjusts focus on the camera, a small shrine object placed carefully on a table beside him, light from a high window tracing every line.

dialogue.speaker: bir_chandra_manikya
dialogue.text: The gods have their rites. Let us give their worship a memory on glass.

i18n.hi: देवताओं की अपनी विधि है; उनकी पूजा को हम काँच पर याद दे दें।

panels.shot: cut to a Calcutta interior: a learned gathering with Tagore-esque literati, then back to his desk piled with books and prints
panels.action: A parallel image shows Calcutta literati debating in a smoke-filled room, copies of journals on a table, while in Agartala Bir Chandra sits at his own desk with Bengali books and stacks of his photographs side by side.

dialogue.text: In Bengal’s cities, writers like Rabindranath Tagore wrestled with kings, devotion and duty in works such as Mukuta, Rajarshi and Visarjan, shaped in part by ties to Tripura’s courtly world.

i18n.hi: बँगाल के शहरों में रवीन्द्रनाथ टैगोर जैसे लेखक मुकुट, राजर्षि और विसर्जन जैसी रचनाओं में राजा, भक्ति और कर्तव्य से जूझ रहे थे, जिन पर त्रिपुरा के दरबारी संसार से रिश्तों की छाप थी।

panels.shot: close-up of his face as he reads a printed Bengali book, with one of his own portraits lying open beside it
panels.action: By the window, Bir Chandra reads a Bengali volume, his eyes pausing on a passage about a troubled king, while beside the book lies one of his portraits—his own royal profile in stiff collar and turban.

dialogue.text: These stories were not his biography. Yet their questioning kings and solemn temples echoed his own balancing act—between throne and conscience, tradition and the strange new gaze of the camera.

i18n.hi: ये कथाएँ उसकी जीवनी नहीं थीं, पर उनके सवाल पूछते राजा और गम्भीर मंदिर उसके अपने संतुलन जैसे थे—सिंहासन और अन्तरात्मा के बीच, परम्परा और कैमरे की अजीब नई नज़र के बीच।

panels.shot: medium shot of an envelope from the Royal Photographic Society on his table, his hand opening it
panels.action: On a neatly arranged desk, an envelope stamped with the crest of the Royal Photographic Society lies beside a little pile of mounted prints, as Bir Chandra’s ringed hand reaches to break its seal.

dialogue.text: By the 1890s, his work travelled beyond the hills. The records of the Royal Photographic Society would one day list him as a Fellow, the hill king counted among an international brotherhood of photographers.

i18n.hi: १८९० के दशक तक उसकी तस्वीरें पहाड़ों से बाहर निकल गईं। रॉयल फ़ोटोग्राफ़िक सोसाइटी के अभिलेखों ने एक दिन उसे फ़ेलो लिखा—पहाड़ी राजा को अंतरराष्ट्रीय फ़ोटोग्राफ़रों की जमात में गिना।

panels.shot: time-lapse style view: the studio dark and dusty decades later, with cobwebs, then faint figures of archivists rediscovering glass plates
panels.action: The same Foto ka Karkhana lies silent decades later, camera shrouded in dust, cobwebs hanging from racks; faint silhouettes of modern archivists lift forgotten glass plates, turning them carefully to the light.

dialogue.text: Long after Bir Chandra’s death in 1896, the Foto ka Karkhana slept behind locked doors. A century later, its camera and glass plates resurfaced, mute yet clear witnesses to his royal experiment with light.

i18n.hi: १८९६ में वीरचंद्र की मौत के बहुत बाद, फ़ोटो का कारख़ाना ताले के पीछे सोया रहा। एक सदी बाद उसका कैमरा और काँच की प्लेटें फिर निकलीं—खामोश, पर साफ़ गवाह, उसके रोशनी वाले शाही तजुर्बे के।

panels.shot: final contemplative shot: over-the-shoulder of Bir Chandra in the studio, looking at a contact sheet of town, school, ritual, and faces
panels.action: From behind Bir Chandra’s shoulder, we see his hands lay out several photographs on a table—a street of Agartala, a classroom, a priest, a courtly portrait—each image catching the same quiet, even light.

dialogue.text: Bir Chandra Manikya did not merely import machines; he made curiosity itself an institution. In his planned town, his academy and his palace photo factory, a hill kingdom stepped into modernity one careful exposure at a time.

i18n.hi: वीरचंद्र माणिक्य ने सिर्फ़ मशीनें नहीं मँगाईं, उसने जिज्ञासा को ही संस्था बना दिया। उसकी बसाई नगरी, उसकी अकादमी और उसकी महल की फोटो फैक्टरी में, एक पहाड़ी राज्य हर सावधान शटर के साथ आधुनिकता में कदम रखता गया।

title_i18n.en: Bir Chandra Opens the Photo Factory

subtitle_i18n.en: A lens of glass in a kingdom of hills
